anchors.prompt: Same kitchen photo, at lunchtime: on the counter a bowl of hot vegetable soup, a plate with scrambled eggs on toast, a bowl of green salad, the cutting board with a small pile of freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley, a glass of water. He stands behind the counter holding a pinch of chopped parsley over the soup, looking at the viewer. Everything else identical — do NOT add any book or aloe.
Same kitchen: he has sprinkled chopped parsley over the soup and holds the spoon, looking at the viewer.

Close-up of a plate with scrambled eggs on toast on the marble counter, his fingers holding a pinch of chopped fresh parsley just above it. Only hand visible. Same place, same light and same objects as the first image, now seen in close-up.
Same close-up: bright green chopped parsley now scattered over the scrambled eggs, his fingers moving away.
Same kitchen, wide: he takes a bite of the scrambled eggs with parsley with a fork, chewing, amused, looking at the viewer.
Same kitchen: he points the fork toward the viewer, shaking his head with a small smile.
Same kitchen: he taps the rim of the plate of eggs with one finger, explaining.
Same kitchen: he opens both hands over the food on the counter, a practical smile.

Close-up of a plate with a piece of grilled white fish on the marble counter, a small glass bowl of green parsley sauce with olive oil beside it, his hand holding a spoon full of the sauce above the fish. Same place, same light and same objects as the first image, now seen in close-up.
Same close-up: the green parsley sauce is drizzled over the fish, shiny olive oil, the spoon moving away.
Same kitchen, wide: he holds the small glass bowl of green parsley sauce, smiling at the viewer.
Same kitchen: he taps the counter with one finger, counting days, explaining.
Same kitchen: he holds up a small pinch of parsley between his fingers, laughing.
Same kitchen: he leans with both hands on the counter, serious, looking straight at the viewer.
Same kitchen: he holds up the small parsley bunch, serious caring face.
Same kitchen: he makes a calming gesture with one open palm, reassuring face.
Same kitchen: he holds up two fingers, calm and clear.
Same kitchen: he mimes drinking from a huge imaginary glass with an ironic raised eyebrow.
Same kitchen: he smiles warmly with four fingers up, then relaxed.

clips.text: Porque la piel se arma desde adentro. Y el perejil fresco, comido, es de las fuentes más baratas de vitamina C que hay.
clips.action: He sprinkles the pinch of chopped parsley over the soup and looks up at the viewer while talking.

clips.text: Dos cucharadas picadas al día. Arriba de la sopa, en la ensalada, en los huevos revueltos. Crudo, al final.
clips.action: Close-up: his fingers sprinkle chopped fresh parsley over scrambled eggs on toast, then over a green salad.

clips.text: Crudo, porque el calor le quita buena parte de la vitamina C. Si lo hierves media hora en el guiso, ya no es lo mismo.
clips.action: He swallows, points the fork at the viewer, and mimes a pot boiling with his other hand, shaking his head.

clips.text: Y otra cosa: el colágeno se hace con proteína. Si comes poca, y después de los sesenta pasa mucho, el perejil solo no alcanza.
clips.action: He puts the fork down and raises an index finger, then taps the plate of eggs.

clips.text: Un huevo, un poco de pollo, lentejas, un yogur. Eso, junto con el perejil. No es magia, es materia prima.
clips.action: He points one by one at the eggs, the soup and the yogurt cup, then opens both hands.

clips.text: Otra forma que me gusta: una salsa verde, con aceite de oliva, un diente de ajo y mucho perejil. Arriba del pescado, de la carne.
clips.action: Close-up: a spoon drizzles a rustic green parsley and olive-oil sauce over a piece of grilled white fish on a plate.

clips.text: Y la vitamina C el cuerpo no la guarda. Por eso es mejor un poquito todos los días, que mucho un día solo.
clips.action: He puts the bowl down and taps the counter rhythmically with his finger as if counting days.

clips.text: ¿Y en el jugo verde de la mañana? Un puñadito está bien. Un puñadito, eh, no el atado entero.
clips.action: He shows a small pinch of parsley with his fingers, then pretends to hold a whole bunch and shakes his head, laughing.

clips.text: Ahora, las advertencias. Y te pido que no te las saltes, porque son importantes.
clips.action: He wipes his hands on a kitchen towel, puts it down and leans on the counter, serious.

clips.text: El perejil tiene mucha vitamina K. Si tomas anticoagulantes, como la warfarina, comer mucho de golpe puede cambiar el efecto del remedio.
clips.action: He speaks slowly and clearly, holding up the small bunch of parsley in one hand as he talks.

clips.text: No quiere decir que no puedas comerlo. Quiere decir que lo hables con tu médico antes, y que no cambies la cantidad de un día para otro.
clips.action: He puts the parsley down, makes a calming gesture with his palm, and nods.

clips.text: Si tienes problemas de riñón, también consulta primero. Y en el embarazo, grandes cantidades de perejil no se recomiendan.
clips.action: He counts two more warnings on his fingers, calm and clear.

clips.text: Una ramita en la ensalada no es el problema. El problema es tomarse litros de jugo de perejil porque alguien dijo que desintoxica.
clips.action: He picks a single sprig and drops it on the salad with a relaxed smile, then mimes drinking a huge glass with an ironic face.

clips.text: Y en la piel, ya lo dijimos: prueba del parche, de noche, sin sol, lejos de los ojos. Con eso estás cuidada.
clips.action: He counts the four rules on his fingers, smiling warmly at the end.
